description: Solo team from the Philippines taking on the MODIS–VIIRS hotspot challenge with AI-assisted development.
summary:
Did the burning change, or did the satellite change? The 2002–2026 hotspot record passes through three satellites, and a change of satellite can look like a change in fire. ARGALLAX is a web tool built on NASA FIRMS that puts the record on one scale and shows how far to trust it.

Choose an area and get a years × months calendar. Each month is compared with its historical reference range and labelled with the satellite that recorded it. Data downloads as CSV.

A record that switches from Aqua MODIS to S-NPP VIIRS in 2012 shows a 5.2-fold jump in yearly totals, yet Aqua's own record shows no rise across the same periods: the jump is a sensor artifact. ARGALLAX never sums satellites. It converts Aqua history to estimated VIIRS-equivalent values with eight ratios fitted on 2012–2017, and continues with NOAA-20 after S-NPP.

The test design was written before any model was fitted. On 18 months not used for fitting or selection (Jan 2020 – Jun 2021), scaling cut the difference from S-NPP in regional monthly totals from 85% to 16%.

We report the limits. The selection rule was changed after selection scores were seen, before the final test; under the original rule, no correction would have been chosen. Eight ratios were not shown better than one, and single cells did not improve.

Counts cover a rectangular area around the Philippines, not the national boundary. Detections are not fire counts or burned area, and agreement with S-NPP is not agreement with ground truth.
details:
THE PROBLEM

The NASA FIRMS hotspot record for the Philippines runs from 2002 to today, but no single satellite covers it. S-NPP ended on 2 November 2026, so any long record now crosses two satellite changes.

ARGALLAX is for analysts, researchers and educators who compare fire seasons across years. Aqua MODIS recorded the early years; S-NPP VIIRS, a sharper sensor, took over in 2012; NOAA-20 VIIRS now continues it.

Aqua records about 6 times fewer cell-days than S-NPP. Joined naively, the record shows a 5.2-fold jump in yearly totals at 2012, while Aqua's own record shows no rise across the same periods.

Anyone reading that record has to ask: did the burning change, or did the satellite change?

ARGALLAX keeps the satellite visible in every month it shows, puts the record on one tested scale, and says plainly what that scale cannot tell you.

WHAT IT DOES

Live site: https://kennethmejes-web.github.io/argallax/

  • Select an area (presets, a drawn box or coordinates) and a date range.
  • See a years × months hotspot calendar from 2002 on one consistent scale.
  • Each month is compared with its historical reference range (10th–90th percentile of the same calendar month in other years) and flagged if it falls outside. This is descriptive, not a prediction or significance test.
  • A band shows which satellite recorded each period. Values before February 2012 are labelled "estimated VIIRS-equivalent"; months from August 2026 are labelled provisional and are never counted as confirmed unusual months. A partial current month is compared only with the same elapsed days in past years.
  • A map shows the detections as each satellite recorded them, not converted, for the selected month, year or a typical year.
  • The yearly record can be switched between "as each satellite recorded it" and "on one scale", so the 2012 satellite change is visible directly.
  • Calendar and hotspot data download as CSV. A Method & limitations panel explains every number.

It is a static website with no server and no accounts, and its numbers can be rebuilt from the FIRMS archive with three commands.

HOW IT WORKS

The unit is daytime grid-cell-days: a 0.25° cell on one UTC day counts once if it has at least one qualifying detection (FIRMS type 0; MODIS confidence ≥ 30; VIIRS excluding low confidence).

The record never adds satellites together. Aqua MODIS history is converted to the S-NPP VIIRS scale with eight ratios, one per latitude band (North Luzon, South Luzon, Visayas, Mindanao) and season (dry: February–May; rest: June–January), fitted on 2012–2017.

NOAA-20 continues the record after S-NPP.

HOW IT WAS TESTED

The test design, periods, scoring and success rule were written before any model was fitted. Ratios were fitted on 2012–2017, the method was chosen on 2018–2019, and the result was tested once on 18 months not used for fitting or method selection (January 2020 – June 2021).

  • 85% → 16%: Scaling cut the difference from S-NPP in regional monthly totals from 85% to 16% of the total. The whole-area total came out 4% low; unscaled Aqua was 85% low.
  • Uncertainty: Whole-area intervals are nominal 80%: 13 of 18 test months fell inside. Regional intervals covered 67%.
  • NOAA-20 continuation: NOAA-20 passed its preregistered tolerance as a continuation of S-NPP for whole-area totals in 2022 – July 2026, reading about 4% higher.

WHAT WE DISCLOSE

  • Method-selection change: The method-selection rule was changed after the 2018–2019 selection scores were seen and before the final test. Under the original rule, no correction would have been selected. Both outcomes are in the record.
  • Model complexity: The test does not show that eight ratios are better than one.
  • Small-area accuracy: For single 0.25° cells, the scaled record was no closer to S-NPP than raw Aqua. No minimum area size is validated.
  • Historical assumption: Values before 2012 assume the 2012–2017 relation held from 2002, which cannot be tested.
  • Sensor instability: After mid-2021 the Aqua-to-S-NPP relation was noisier; the cause cannot be separated between Aqua's orbit drift, S-NPP aging and real change.
  • NOAA-20 validation: NOAA-20 was not checked by region or season in the preregistered test, and cannot be checked after S-NPP ended.
  • Cloud cover: Clouds are not corrected for.
  • Ground truth: All agreement is with S-NPP VIIRS detections, not with true fire activity. Hotspot detections are not fire counts or burned area, and no detections does not mean no fire. Counts cover a rectangular screening area around the Philippines, not the national boundary.

WHAT IT CANNOT TELL YOU

Whether burning rose, fell or stayed the same.

It shows where the record changes satellite, which values were converted, and how well the conversion tested.

TOOLS AND AI USE

Tools: Python (data pipeline and analysis); Vite, TypeScript, MapLibre GL JS, d3-scale-chromatic and topojson-client (website); Natural Earth (basemap); Source Sans 3 (website) and IBM Plex (slides) fonts.

License: Code is Apache-2.0.

Creator: ARGALLAX was created by Kenneth Mejes for Project Sidequest, a solo entry in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

AI disclosure: Development was AI-assisted, with the project direction, scientific decisions, and final accountability held by the creator. AI tools used: Claude and Claude Code (Anthropic); ChatGPT and Codex (OpenAI).
